To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sequential changes in nuclear DNA content of gastric cancer cells in dogs treated with mitomycin C were correlated with the oncostatic effect of the agent.
chemotherapy with M-83 reduced the nuclear DNA content of gastric carcinoma in dogs.
the nuclear DNA contents of the tumor cells in dogs with gastric cancer were reduced after chemotherapy, and this change correlated with the histological findings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sequential changes of nuclear DNA contents of gastric carcinoma induced by N- ethyl-N′- nitro-N-nitroso-guanidine (ENGN) in beagle dogs.
the sequential changes in the nuclear DNA content of gastric cancer caused by chemotherapy in dogs.
the effects of chemotherapy on the nuclear DNA content of tumor cells in experimental canine gastric cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M-83 has an inhibitory effect on the proliferation of gastric cancer cells and that this effect is reflected in sequential changes in the nuclear DNA content.
the nuclear DNA histogram of gastric cancer cells in dogs treated with M-83 changed sequentially from a heterogeneous pattern to a homogeneous one.
the nuclear DNA distribution of gastric cancer cells in the chemotherapy-effective cases changed to a normal pattern, and the nuclear DNA content of the cells decreased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear DNA distribution of the cancer cell is a useful index for the objective evaluation of the effect of oncostatic agents.
the nuclear DNA distribution is an objective and sensitive parameter for the evaluation of the oncostic effect of M-83 in canine gastric cancer.
the nuclear DNA histogram of the gastric carcinoma in dogs is useful as an objective parameter for the evaluation of oncostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that a simple change in the chemical structure of a compound can lead to a significant increase in its ability to induce DNA damage in cells.
it is not enough to have a single metric for the success of a project, such as the number of publications.
the use of DNA content as a marker of tumor progression is a useful tool in the management of patients with advanced gastric cancer.
